parsed.title: Sensor re-implements the routing decision instead of projecting the router's table
parsed.detail: The doc comment claims "The router (scripts/unit-route.mjs) owns the class→route decision; this surface projects it", but readSuggestions decides with its own free-text heuristic: PLAN_ROUTE = /replan[- ]in[- ]unit|owned by plan|plan owner|plan-owner/i tested against the raw route/klass cells, then a fallback that sends ANY open row to /fold-findings. This is exactly the divergent-implementations defect #224 exists to close (the drift test's own comment cites the "three-contradictory-sentences defect"). Concrete contradictions: (a) review-loop-discipline.test.mjs §7 pins the resolution map "class `plan` → `plan-feature`", but a row with class `plan` and a route cell like "fold into phase" fails PLAN_ROUTE and gets the /fold-findings suggestion; (b) a decision-class open row (fold-findings pins "decision-required") is routed to /fold-findings by the sensor while the router's closed ROUTES table routes decision rows to "decision". Two machines now publish two different answers for the same ledger.

parsed.title: Trigger text hardcodes 'replan-in-unit' for non-replan matches
parsed.detail: trigger: `an open finding's frozen route is the plan owner — replan-in-unit (${...})` is emitted even when the row matched via klass or via the 'owned by plan'/'plan owner' alternatives of PLAN_ROUTE, i.e. when no row's route is replan-in-unit. The machine publishes a route name the row does not carry — the machine→text failure mode the repo's own AC15 gate defines ("the machine publishes a value that no normative surface names").

parsed.title: Pinned version assertion edited, contradicting the file's own immutability contract
parsed.detail: The diff rewrites the existing pin from assert.match(foldSkill, /version: 1\.4\.0/) to /version: 1\.5\.0/. The same file asserts (section 9, O22/O23) that tests are immutable once written and the sole legitimate amendment is "a proven mis-encoding of external semantic" cited from authoritative documentation; the header also states tests "are never edited to pass". A skill version bump is not a mis-encoding of external semantics, and the new comment self-acknowledges the edit ("fix #224 moved it 1.4.0 → 1.5.0") rather than meeting the stated exception. The repo's own contract requires surfacing this as a finding + SPEC amendment, not silently rewriting the expectation.

parsed.title: Header's fixture claim contradicted by the determinism/git-status tests
parsed.detail: The file header states "every fixture is either the committed tree at scripts/fixtures/unit-route/ or a copy of it under os.tmpdir()", but the AC4 tests run the router against the live repository itself (run(["224-deterministic-replan-routing"], { root: null }) with cwd: repoRoot and no UNIT_ROUTE_REPO), which is neither the fixture tree nor a tmpdir copy — and the git-status test executes the router in the developer's real, possibly dirty checkout, so "a run leaves git status --porcelain unchanged" is only checked against whatever state happens to exist.
